title: Organization invitations
description: Tenant invitations for multi-tenant apps: invite by email with a role, inspect, accept once, revoke and expire, with hashed one-time tokens, injected authorization and persistence, and a Fetch Request/Response adapter.

notes: Requires a TypeScript build and Web Crypto (crypto.subtle, getRandomValues, randomUUID) plus the Fetch Request/Response APIs: Node.js 22+, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Next.js route handlers and Hono.
Framework-neutral core; mount the HTTP adapter with your framework's catch-all route.
No runtime packages, environment reads, timers or network activity at install or import time.

configuration: On PostgreSQL, apply schema.sql and use createSqlInvitationStore with your query executor, passing onAccepted to insert the membership row in the accepting transaction; on other databases implement InvitationStore with a unique token_hash and a conditional status update.
Implement authorize(actor, action, {tenantId, role}) from your own membership table and enforce role ceilings there (who may invite whom).
Declare the invitable roles; keep owner or billing roles out unless invitations should grant them.
Implement authenticate(request) from your session or verified token; verifiedEmail must come from your identity provider.
Implement sendInvitation with your email provider and build the join link from a trusted base URL, keeping the token in the URL fragment.
Mount createInvitationHandler under one prefix with exact allowedOrigins; it complements, not replaces, your CSRF policy.
limitations: Does not create memberships, users or tenants; your store's accepted transition must do that atomically.
Does not send email or render templates; failed delivery revokes the invitation so nothing is left pending.
The in-memory store is for tests and prototypes only; the SQL store is tested on PostgreSQL semantics through PGlite, not on every hosted Postgres.
No rate limiting beyond the per-tenant pending cap; add request rate limits (see the rate-limit module) on invite and accept routes.
Production database correctness, session security, email deliverability and consuming-application acceptance remain project responsibilities.
decisions: routes: POST {prefix}, GET {prefix}?tenantId=, DELETE {prefix}/{id}, POST {prefix}/inspect, POST {prefix}/accept
accepting a used invite → 409 already-accepted; expired or revoked → 410
token stored as SHA-256 hash; re-inviting an email revokes the earlier link
failed email send revokes the invite → 502 delivery-failed
options: ttlMs: invite lifetime (default 7 days); maxPendingPerTenant (default 100, then 429)
requireEmailMatch: verified email must equal the invited one (default true, mismatch → 403)

verification.command: npm run build && node --test tests/org-invitations.test.mjs tests/org-invitations-sql.test.mjs
behaviors: invite returns a 256-bit token once and stores only its SHA-256 hash
accept succeeds once; replays fail with already-accepted
exactly one of several concurrent accepts wins
expired, revoked, unknown and malformed tokens fail with distinct codes
re-inviting an email revokes the earlier link
members, admins of another tenant and role ceilings are refused
a different signed-in account cannot use a forwarded link (email-mismatch)
pending invitations are capped per tenant
HTTP adapter: status codes, origin check, minimal inspect response, revoke and failed-delivery revocation
schema.sql applies and the SQL store passes the core behaviors on PostgreSQL
four concurrent accepts against the database have exactly one winner
onAccepted inserts the membership in the accepting transaction; a failing insert rolls the accept back

changes: Add schema.sql (PostgreSQL) and createSqlInvitationStore with transactional onAccepted membership creation.
First release: core, in-memory store and Fetch adapter.
